claims.text: The predictive approach is based on machine-learning models.
The models are trained on compositional and structural features of high-entropy alloys.
The approach can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Accurate identification is enabled by leveraging the interplay between elemental properties and lattice distortions.
The approach is trained on a diverse dataset of high-entropy alloys.
The approach is validated using experimental data.
Lattice distortions and elemental properties are the structural mediators used by the approach.
The approach captures relationships between compositional and structural features.
Capturing compositional–structural relationships enables accurate identification of low-phonon-thermal-conductivity materials.
The approach will outperform current predictive methods by at least 15% in accuracy.
Use of the approach has the potential to yield a reduction in phonon thermal conductivity of up to 20%.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys whose compositions and structures are similar to those represented in the training dataset.
Model accuracy may depend on the quality and diversity of the training dataset.
Model accuracy may be affected by the complexity of relationships between compositional and structural features.
A deviation greater than 10% between measured and predicted phonon thermal conductivity is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention only applies a predictive approach to identify materials, but the outcome states that phonon thermal conductivity itself may be reduced by up to 20%. A prediction method does not directly alter conductivity unless a material-selection or modification intervention is specified.

The predicted improvement is defined as at least 15% greater accuracy than current methods, whereas falsification is based only on absolute prediction error exceeding 10%; the experiment does not directly test the claimed 15% comparative improvement.
